title: Marguerite and the Compass
premise: When a dying prospector presses a hand-drawn map into his hands, blacklisted mountain guide Theo Ashgrove inherits more than a route to a lost silver vein — he inherits the prospector's estranged daughter, Marguerite, who arrives demanding her birthright and answers about the father who abandoned her. Pursued by the mining syndicate that killed the old man and betrayed Theo twenty years ago, they cross the range ahead of the early snows, discovering the map leads not just to silver but to evidence of the syndicate's crimes. At the summit pass, with the storm closing in, Theo must choose between the vein that could buy back his name and the testimony that could bring justice; he burns the map's treasure half and delivers the ledger to a frontier judge, clearing his record at last — not by law's grace, but by proof. Marguerite, having found belonging in the crossing rather than the inheritance, stays on as his partner in a new guiding outfit.
about_author: Vesper Hartwell is the pen name of a former alpine rescue volunteer who now writes adventure fiction from a cabin above the tree line. Their work explores how wild places strip people down to what they truly owe one another.

chapters.title: The Dying Man's Bargain
chapters.summary: Theo Ashgrove, guiding one last season before winter, finds prospector Elias Wren gut-shot in a high meadow. With his final breaths, Elias trades a weathered map for a promise: see it through, and find my daughter. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: reluctant obligation — a man who trusts no one agreeing to carry a stranger's dying wish.

chapters.title: A Daughter Arrives
chapters.summary: Marguerite Wren storms into the valley town asking after her father, armed only with a decade-old letter. Theo, honoring the promise, tells her everything except the map's destination. She demands to come. POV: Marguerite. Emotional beat: anger masking grief — she wants inheritance and an apology in equal measure.

chapters.title: Men in Good Coats
chapters.summary: Syndicate agents arrive in town wearing respectable faces, asking the same questions Marguerite did. Theo recognizes their leader, Callum Reeve, from the betrayal that got him blacklisted twenty years ago. They slip out of town at night. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: old fear resurfacing — the past has teeth and it is hunting.

chapters.title: The Low Trail
chapters.summary: They take the forested low route to avoid patrols, and Marguerite proves tougher than Theo expected, reading her father's marginalia like a second language. A near-drowning at a swollen ford forces grudging trust. POV: Marguerite. Emotional beat: first flicker of belonging — competence earning respect instead of suspicion.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Says
chapters.summary: Sheltering in an abandoned trapper's cabin, they discover the map conceals a folded page of Elias's ledger: dates, payments, and names proving the syndicate murdered claim-jumpers — including Marguerite's mother. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into purpose; this is no longer about silver.

chapters.title: Reeve's Offer
chapters.summary: Reeve corners them at a river crossing with a proposal: the map for Marguerite's safe passage and Theo's name cleared. Theo nearly takes it; Marguerite refuses for both of them. They scatter his horses and climb higher. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: temptation and shame — twenty years of exile weighed against one clean betrayal.

chapters.title: Above the Tree Line
chapters.summary: The real climb begins: scree, cold, thin air, and snow arriving weeks early. Marguerite falters with altitude sickness, and Theo carries her through a whiteout to a cave, confessing the full story of his blacklist while she shivers against the rock. POV: Marguerite. Emotional beat: vulnerability exchanged for trust — the father-shaped hole acknowledged.

chapters.title: The Vein
chapters.summary: They reach the silver seam at dawn — a fortune glittering in blue ice. Theo samples it, calculates what it would mean, and watches Reeve's climbing party ascending toward them. The choice crystallizes: take the ore or take the ledger to the judge at Fort Meridian, two days down the far slope. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: clarity — some inheritances are debts, not gifts.

chapters.title: The Pass
chapters.summary: Climax. In the storm-bound pass, Theo collapses a cornice across Reeve's route, buying hours but trapping himself and Marguerite above. They descend the killer chute Elias once survived, Marguerite leading by her father's notes while Theo fights a broken arm. Reeve falls pursuing them; the mountain keeps its own justice. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: terror and resolve — each saving the other.

chapters.title: Measured in Miles
chapters.summary: At Fort Meridian, the ledger lands before Judge Corliss; warrants go out, and Theo's name is formally restored. Marguerite buries her father's letters at the trailhead and signs on as Theo's partner for spring routes. The last line measures the year ahead in miles, together. POV: Marguerite. Emotional beat: quiet resolution — belonging found not inherited, justice won outside the law's waiting rooms.
